Bonding and Grounding: PBB, SBB, TBB, BCT, and What Gets Bonded

Unit 3: Pathways and Spaces. Lesson 13 of 52 in INST1 Academy.

A storm takes out a switch in a building that passed inspection last year. The cause is not the cable, it is the difference in electrical potential between two rooms. Telecom bonding exists to keep that difference small. The busbars, the conductors between them, and the bonds to racks and pathways together make up the telecommunications bonding infrastructure.

Why bond

Bonding joins metal parts so they sit at the same electrical potential. It also gives fault and surge current a deliberate, low-resistance path instead of letting it find one through a person or a cable. Grounding connects to the earth; bonding joins metal to metal. Telecom needs both.

The parts

Part                                   What it does
PBB (formerly TMGB)                    one per building; in the EF; bonded to the service ground
BCT                                    connects the PBB to the electrical service's grounding electrode system; keep short
TBB                                    insulated stranded copper from the PBB to each SBB
SBB (formerly TGB)                     one or more per TR or ER, in each room
Rack bonding conductor (formerly TEBC) 6 AWG minimum, from the busbar to each rack
Grounding equalizer                    6 AWG minimum between TRs, evening out potentials

The BCT connects the PBB to the electrical service's grounding electrode system, the TBB links the SBBs on each floor, and each rack gets its own conductor back to the nearest busbar.

What gets bonded

  • Racks and cabinets
  • Cable tray, ladder rack, and metal conduit
  • Cable shields and armored cable
  • The entrance protector

Use green, or green with a yellow stripe, for every bonding conductor.

What not to do

Never use the water pipe as the telecom ground path on its own. Never rely on a power cord ground as the only ground for a rack. The telecom ground path is separate and verifiable.

Tip: copy the old name next to the new on your notes. The exam and some drawings use both.
Exam tip: the PBB is formerly the TMGB and the SBB is formerly the TGB. The TBB goes from the PBB to the SBBs, and the BCT connects the PBB to the electrical service's grounding electrode system.
Remember
PBB in the entrance room, TBB up the building to each SBB, BCT to the electrode, and a green conductor to every rack, tray, and shield.
Deeper explanation

Bonding and Grounding: PBB, SBB, TBB, BCT, and What Gets Bonded, explained slowly

A bonding layout for a three-floor building

A building has an entrance facility in the basement and a TR on each of three floors, each with two racks. This is the plan, from the service entrance to the last rack.

Link                        From               To                   Conductor
BCT                         building service   PBB in the EF        shortest route
TBB segment 1               PBB                SBB in TR 1          insulated stranded copper
TBB segment 2               PBB                SBB in TR 2          insulated stranded copper
TBB segment 3               PBB                SBB in TR 3          insulated stranded copper
Rack bonding conductors     SBB in each TR     each rack            6 AWG minimum, 6 in total
Equalizer                   TR 1 SBB           TR 3 SBB             6 AWG minimum, if designed

The BCT connects the PBB to the electrical service's grounding electrode system and is kept as short as possible. The TBB links the PBB to each SBB so every floor is at the same potential. The rack bonding conductor (formerly TEBC) is a 6 AWG minimum, stranded, insulated copper conductor from the SBB to each rack. Every bonding conductor is green, or green with a yellow stripe.

Count the labels

Each bonding conductor is labeled at both ends.

Conductors              Count   Labels (2 per conductor)
BCT                     1       2
TBB segments            3       6
Rack conductors         6       12
Total                           20

What else gets bonded

  • Every rack and cabinet, each by its own conductor.
  • Ladder rack and cable tray sections.
  • Metal conduit, through a grounding bushing and a 6 AWG copper wire to the busbar.
  • Cable shields and armored cable.
  • The entrance protector.

Names to know

The primary bonding busbar is formerly the TMGB. The secondary bonding busbar is formerly the TGB. The rack bonding conductor is formerly the TEBC. If a document shows an old name, translate it before you act.

What not to do

Do not use a water pipe as the only telecom ground path, because plastic pipe or a meter breaks the path without anyone noticing. Do not daisy-chain rack to rack, because one loose joint drops every rack after it. Do not rely on a power cord ground as the only ground for a rack.

Remember: PBB in the basement, TBB to each floor, an SBB in each room, and one conductor to each rack.
